name: the heading is resolved by a previousElementSibling walk again
why: Defect 1 verbatim. MusicBrainz wraps a merge-able listing's table in <form><nav>, so a sibling walk runs out of siblings inside the wrapper and _relCreateRetryButtons() discards the button. The <form>-wrapped test must go from 'a direct child of the H2' to 'the control exists' failing outright.

name: the insertion point is button:last-of-type again
why: Defect 2 verbatim. On an <h3> carrying a sub-table filter that selector resolves to #mb-stf-<col>-clear, several levels deep, so the control lands inside span.mb-stf-input-wrap. The multi-table test asserts the parent IS the h3, so it must fail. Note the single-table test can also see this, which is why both are listed separately below.

name: the insertion point is button:last-of-type again (single-table arm)
why: The same mutation seen from the other page shape: on the <form>-wrapped h2 the selector resolves into #mb-filter-container, so the control is no longer a direct child of the heading. Listed separately because the two page shapes fail it for different reasons and a fix for one would not necessarily fix the other.

name: the control is inserted at the heading's end instead of its control run
why: The plausible simplification: 'just append it to the heading'. It survives every existence check and puts the control after the global filter bar on an h2 — outside the row of controls it is meant to join, and out of reach of updateH2Count()'s re-anchor ordering. The position assertion (immediately after .mb-row-count-stat) is the only thing that sees it.

name: the multi-table <h2> guard is dropped
why: An honest expect: "pass". The guard keeps a per-table control off the PAGE heading, which belongs to #mb-rel-retry-global. No committed multi-table fixture can exercise it: caaFindHeaderForTable() tries findH3ForTable() first, and on every multi-table fixture here renderGroupedTable() puts an h3.mb-toggle-h3 immediately before each table, so the h2 fallback is never reached and removing the guard changes nothing. Reproducing it needs a multi-table page whose sub-table has no h3 within five element-siblings — which would be a rendering bug in its own right. Recorded rather than left unmentioned.
